placements.why: The envelope's entire content is a system-design decision (an async job contract for the remember operation) treated as a ratified, binding specification. Nothing in the empty strata or graph covers organizational content of this shape — a foundational architecture category is the legible home, minted standalone since no ancestor category exists yet and none is required.
placements.title: System design commitments are ratified as explicit contracts
placements.frame: What guarantees does a named architectural mechanism make, and were they formally settled or merely assumed?

placements.title: Async operations are specified as contracts with named guarantees, not left implicit
placements.frame: What does the ratified contract promise about return timing, work durability under client failure, and how the caller ultimately receives the result?
placements.why: src-1 announces the ratification and names the mechanism (receipt returned in seconds, cursor-polled extraction); src-2 asserts the properties that follow from the design (no blocking, no lost work on dropped receipts); src-3 restates the settled dispatch/poll-or-piggyback pattern as the 'key decision.' All three converge on the same subject — the contract's guarantees — which is a theme future envelopes about this or other async contracts will keep feeding, not a one-time fact. The grain test admits it: this names a recurring subject (contract guarantees for async operations), not a single measurement or event.
